checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.item: One finished 16:9 image with original left and renovated right
must.why: Final image is roughly 5:3 and the left panel is a cropped, regenerated version, not the supplied photo.

must.item: Left photo retains brown cabinets, beige tiles and original clutter
must.why: Brown cabinets and beige tiles are kept, but the left side is cropped and altered. The clutter is reduced, the left counter is changed to a marble-like top, and the right sink is gone.

must.item: Right panel has white shaker cabinets, light oak counters, white subway tiles, uncluttered
must.why: White shaker cabinets, oak butcher-block counters, white tiles and clear counters are all there.

must.item: Generated kitchen preserves geometry, fixtures and viewpoint
must.why: The standalone version matches the layout well. In the composite the right panel is cropped and squeezed, and the left counter is missing.
Both labels are legible and sit within the correct panels.

faults.what: The Before panel is a regenerated, cropped version of the original. The clutter is mostly gone, the left counter looks like marble, and the right sink is missing.
Each panel is cropped, so the composition and layout no longer match the original photo.
The After side loses the corner and right side view, which makes the room look different.
The labels are large and heavy, and they cover part of the cabinets.

summary: The standalone renovation is good, but the before-and-after composite redraws and crops the original, so the Before side is no longer the user's photo and the layout is distorted.
